newsitem.title: GERMANY: East Germans disappointed by market economy - poll.
newsitem.headline: East Germans disappointed by market economy - poll.

text.p: Eastern Germans are deeply disappointed by the capitalist system they have had for the past six years and many of them look back with nostalgia at life under communism, an opinion poll released on Wednesday showed.

But only about 10 percent of easterners want the communists back and a majority now agree with western economic concepts such as competition and performance-related pay, the survey carried out by the Allensbach Institute said.

The percentage of east Germans with a favourable opinion of the united country's western-style economy has plunged from 77 percent just before unification in 1990 to 22 percent as of last November, it showed.
West Germans have also become more critical of their so-called social market economy, but among them the positive views fell from 57 percent in 1994 to 45 percent last November.

"It is hard to imagine a more dramatic fall than this," Allensbach founder Elisabeth Noelle-Neumann said as she presented the study for the economic weekly Wirtschaftswoche. "Capitalism is seen (in eastern Germany) ever more critically."

But the future need not be so bleak as the figures seem to show, she added, because the east Germans have actually come much closer to west Germans in terms of the underlying values that foster support for a market economy.

There was hardly any difference in the strong support for competition to motivate and inspire employees, with 74 percent of the westerners and 75 percent of the easterners agreeing this was a positive aspect.

At the same time, easterners were markedly critical of capitalism as a system and were more positive towards many aspects of life under communism that they criticised strongly in 1990, the study showed.

More that three-quartes of east Germans now look back at the former communist state as peace-loving and comradely. The percentage of those calling it undemocratic fell from 66 to 39 percent while those criticising it at bureaucratic dropped from 82 to 38 percent.

Noelle-Neumann, the doyenne of German pollsters, said east Germans were apparently still quite confused by the complex economic system they inherited from the west and would take years before they lost their nostalgic view of the past.
